A rocket's position after t seconds is x = 15t and y = -16t² + 32t, in feet. What is its maximum height?

solutionSteps: (a) Solve x = t - 2 for t: t = x + 2. Substitute into y = 5t: y = 5·x + 2 + 0 = 5x + 10. b = 10.
(b) The ball lands when y = 0: -16t² + 16t + 96 = 0. Factor: -16(t - 3)(t + 2) = 0. The landing time is t = 3 s, so x = 25·3 = 75 ft.
(c) Find t: -2t - 1 = -5, so t = 2. Substitute t = 2 into y: y = 11.
(d) y is a downward parabola in t; its vertex is at t = -b/(2a) = -32/(2·(-16)) = 1. y(1) = -16(1)² + 32(1) + 0 = 16. Maximum height: 16 ft.
